_comment: Single source of truth for the camera-support generator's controls. The page builds its sliders from this, the worker converts UI values to metres with `scale`, and the backend clamps anything the assistant proposes to these ranges. Change a range here and all three follow.

sliders.label: Rigidity
sliders.help: How little the camera may move under a 1 g load. 0 allows 2 mm, 50 allows 0.2 mm, 100 allows 0.02 mm. Struts thicken to meet it.

sliders.label: Feet per anchor
sliders.help: How many legs the structure splits into at each anchor point.

sliders.label: Base spread
sliders.help: Radius of the circle the feet land on around each anchor. Wider resists tipping and twisting; feet that would fall off the surface are pulled in. On a ring anchor: the spacing between neighbouring legs along the ring.

sliders.label: Branch point
sliders.help: How far from the camera the trunk divides into legs. Low splits early into a wide tripod; high keeps a single trunk most of the way.

sliders.label: Sweep
sliders.help: How strongly the trunk arcs away from the camera before heading to the base. 0 is a straight run.

sliders.label: Cross ties
sliders.help: Rings of struts joining neighbouring legs. Adds torsional stiffness and the webbed look.

sliders.label: Blend
sliders.help: Size of the fillets where members meet. Small reads as a welded frame, large as a grown form.

sliders.label: Clearance
sliders.help: Gap kept between the structure and anything in the scan, and from the camera's field of view.

sliders.label: Ring width
sliders.help: Width of the base ring, as a share of the flat round face it sits on. 100 covers the face from edge to edge.

sliders.label: Cable room
sliders.help: Straight space kept free behind the camera for the connectors and cables. Nothing is routed through it. Cognex asks for 150 mm before the first bend.

sliders.label: Standoff
sliders.help: Straight neck length behind the camera plate before the trunk starts to curve.

sliders.label: Min strut
sliders.help: Thinnest strut the process can make. Sizing never goes below it.

sliders.label: Max strut
sliders.help: Thickest strut allowed. If the rigidity target needs more, the target is reported as not met.

sliders.label: Plate / floor
sliders.help: Thickness of the camera mounting plate, or of a cradle's or sleeve's floor. Their walls and roof are 0.6 of it, never under 3 mm.

sliders.label: Grip length
sliders.help: How much of the camera body a cradle or sleeve wraps, centred on the bolt pattern. It never reaches the connectors.

_holders: How the support holds the camera. All three bolt to the camera's own M3 pattern; a cradle or sleeve also wraps the body so the camera cannot rock or peel off the screws. They need a camera with a drawn body (body_mm and grip_mm). legacyHolder is what a setup saved before holders existed was drawn with.

holders.label: Plate
holders.help: A flat plate under the camera, held by its four screws alone.

holders.label: Cradle, open top
holders.help: A channel the camera body lies in: floor and two side walls, open above and behind. The four screws go through the floor.

holders.label: Sleeve, camera slides in
holders.help: A closed band round the camera body: floor, walls and roof, open in front and behind. The body slides in connectors first until the light head meets it; the four screws go through the floor.

_cameras: Camera frame for body_mm and mount_mm: x along the view (front face at +x), y across, z up, origin on the optical axis at mid length. body_mm are the solids the support must stay out of; mount_mm is the centre of the bolt pattern on the mounting face. Cameras without body_mm are a plain box of size_mm with the plate centred on the chosen face. grip_mm is the stretch of the body, along x, that a cradle or sleeve may wrap: the housing behind the lens or light head, stopping short of the connectors. It is scaled from the outline drawing, good to about a millimetre.

cameras.label: In-Sight 2800 / 2801 · Multi Torch
cameras.note: Body and bolt pattern from the In-Sight 2800 Reference Manual, p. 19: four M3 holes on the bottom plate, 21.1 × 37.0 mm, threads 4 mm deep. Use screws no longer than the plate thickness plus 4 mm. Weight per Cognex: 290 g in the Multi Torch configuration; a right-angle configuration adds 50 g. The two M12 connectors (power and I/O, Ethernet) leave straight out of the back; Cognex asks for 150 mm of straight cable behind them before the first bend.

cameras.label: In-Sight 2800 · Mini 6.2 mm
cameras.note: Body, bolt pattern and weight from the In-Sight 2800 Reference Manual, p. 16 and 61: four M3 holes on the bottom plate, 21.1 × 37.0 mm, threads 4 mm deep. Use screws no longer than the plate thickness plus 4 mm. The two M12 connectors leave straight out of the back; Cognex asks for 150 mm of straight cable behind them before the first bend.

cameras.label: Custom
cameras.note: Enter the body envelope, mass and hole spacing from the camera's drawing. The plate is centred on the chosen face.

_lenses: fovDeg is the diagonal field of view, from the working-distance tables in the In-Sight 2800 Reference Manual (p. 29–33): the keep-out cone has to contain the whole image, corners included.
